CIVIL JUDGE, KALABURAGI IN MISC. NO.29/2014 ON I.A. FILED U/SEC.151 OF CPC AND ALLOW THE APPLICATION FOR RELEASE.

, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
ORDER Heard Sri R. J. Bhusare, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Sanjeevkumar C. Patil, learned counsel for respondent No.2 and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent Nos.1 and 3.

The present writ petition is filed with the following reliefs:

sentences.text: "i) Issue a writ, direction or order in the nature of certiorari by quashing Annexure-F dated 12.7.2017 passed by the III Addl. Senior Civil Judge, Kalaburagi in Misc.No.29/2014 on I.A. filed U/s 151 of CPC and allow the application for release.

entities.text: III Addl. Senior Civil Judge, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ii) Issue a writ, direction or order in the nature of Mandamus directing the respondents to release the amount as claimed in the application.
iii) Issue a writ, direction or order which deem fit under the fact and circumstances of the case."
3. The petitioner is the land loser having lost his land for the benefit of respondent No.2.
As per Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, an application came to be filed directing the respondents to deposit the compensation amount.
The said application was disposed of.
Thereafter, an application came to be filed by the petitioner for withdrawal of the compensation amount.
The learned Trial Judge by order dated 12.07.2017 has dismissed the application stating that main petition itself is NC: 2024:KHC-K:2233 disposed of.
The said order is called in question by the petitioner in this petition.

4. Having heard the parties, this Court is of the considered opinion that the approach of the Trial Court is incorrect, inasmuch as it is the petitioner who is entitled to receive the compensation and withdraw the amount.

5. If there is any dispute inter-se among the sharers of the compensation, it is always open for the Trial Court to direct the petitioner to seek for reference under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.
No such order is forthcoming on record.
6. Under such circumstances, the order needs to be set aside and the matter needs to be remitted to the Trial Court for fresh disposal in accordance with law.

7. Hence, the following:
ORDER i) The writ petition is allowed.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:2233 ii) The order at Annexure - F dated 12.07.20217 is hereby quashed.
iii) The matter is remitted to the Trial Court for fresh disposal in accordance with law.
